questions.question: A tool returns a 4,000-character report at step 2 of a 10-step run. Which steps pay for it?
options: Every step from 3 onwards, because each call re-sends the whole history
questions.explanation: The observation sits in the history, and the history is re-sent on every later model call.

questions.question: Each step adds about the same number of tokens to the history. How does a run's total input grow with its number of steps N?
questions.explanation: Step n sends about n·k tokens; summing over N steps gives about k·N²/2.

questions.question: Why does the budget warn the model at 80% instead of only stopping at 100%?
options: So the model can wrap up with what it has, instead of being cut off with no answer
questions.explanation: A model that knows it's nearly out of budget can produce a useful final answer.

questions.question: In the measured run, trimming observations to 600 characters changed the real prompt-token total from 2,737 to:
questions.explanation: A 66% cut, because the long report was re-sent at every later step.

questions.question: llama3.2 reported fewer input tokens at step 2 than at step 1, despite a longer history. Why?
options: Ollama caches prompts and doesn't count them
Its chat template only includes tool definitions in the last user message; after a tool result, the tools drop out of the prompt
A bug in this lesson's code
questions.explanation: Token counts depend on the template. This one also hides the tools from the model after its first call.

questions.question: When are token estimates (characters ÷ 4) the right choice for a budget?
options: Only for rough planning, or when the API returns no usage; enforce budgets with reported usage
questions.explanation: Measured here, the estimate was off by 17–30% in both directions.
